title: SLO-guided node-drain smoothing and cross-zone hedging for degraded-GPU nodes
author: Maya L. Chen
body: Summary: Introduces an SLO-driven node drain smoothing controller and cross-zone hedging policy to avoid latency spikes and bulk eviction storms when GPU nodes degrade or enter maintenance. This change reduces p99 latency regressions observed during abrupt node drains by allowing gradual eviction + short-term hedging to nearby healthy zones, with automatic fallbacks to smaller quantized model variants when capacity is constrained. Motivation: Recent incidents (SUP-4421) revealed that immediate eviction of pods on degraded GPU hosts caused transient head-of-line latency increases and cache warm-up penalties across many tenants. Our existing circuit-breaker/eviction logic is binary: evict now or not. This PR implements a middle path that honors SLO envelopes and keeps high-priority requests within budget while draining safely. Design highlights: 1) slo-drain-controller (new component in scheduler): observes node health, request SLO burn-rate (from metrics-exporter), and issues phased eviction directives: MARK_DRAIN_PRE (reduce new routing to node), PHASED_EVICT (evict low-priority pods first), FINAL_EVICT. 2) Cross-zone hedging policy: when draining a node in zone A, the router can optionally route a small percentage of new requests to compatible replicas in zone B/C for a bounded duration (configurable via runtime flag hedging.window_ms and hedging.weight_pct). Hedging stops automatically when the drain phase completes. 3) Temporary model fallback: when aggregate headroom across zones is insufficient, the controller can trigger a short-lived rollout to a compatible, smaller quantized model variant (e.g. 8-bit quantized) for affected routes to preserve latency SLOs. This uses the existing rollout infra with an emergency flag (emergencyModelFallback=true) scoped to customer/route. 4) KV-cache flush & rebind fix: addresses an observed race where pod eviction + near-instant recreate could cause stale KV cache references. The fix ensures an explicit KV cache checkpoint and a brief grace TTL before rebind. 5) Observability: adds metrics slo_drain_phase{phase="pre|phased|final"}, hedged_routes_count, hedging_traffic_pct, fallback_model_active, and a dashboard with p50/p90/p99 and error budget burn. Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (canary, 1% of clusters): enable slo-drain-controller in canary region with hedging.disabled=false but fallback disabled. Monitor error-budget and latency. - Stage 2 (10%): enable cross-zone hedging with hedging.weight_pct=5 and enable fallback for non-SLA tenants. - Stage 3 (global): ramp weight_pct up to 15 for high-priority routes; enable per-tenant tuning. Feature flags and operator docs included. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for controller decision logic and eviction ordering. - Integration tests (simulated node degradation) verifying gradual eviction ordering and hedging routing. - Chaos e2e run: simulated GPU host flapping showed p99 reduced by ~38% vs immediate-eviction baseline in internal perf runs. - KV-cache rebind unit + e2e validated under recreate race. Rollback: feature gates allow immediate disable (hedging.disabled=true, controller off) and automatic rollback of any emergencyModelFallback via rollout engine. If regression detected, operator doc includes steps to revert and to run a forced cache clear across affected nodes. Related changes: small API addition to routing layer (RouteHints.hedgeCandidates and hedgeWeight) and a new admin endpoint /admin/v1/drain_status for on-demand inspection. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by SRE and Runtime teams - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary deployment in internal staging - [x] Observability dashboard and alert: EvictionRateSpike, HedgingErrorRatio - [x] Rollout playbook entry added Notes: This is intentionally conservative on hedging weight and fallback usage for the first public rollout. The goal is to prevent outage amplification during node-level degradations while limiting cross-zone traffic to a predictable budget.

review_comments: Adrian Park (2026-02-23): Left a few nits but overall this looks solid. Can we add a guard that prevents hedging for routes with strict geo requirements?
Maya L. Chen (2026-02-23): Added a geo-constraint check in router; updated tests. See commit 9b8d7e5.
Sofia Martinez (2026-02-24): Please call out the operational cost estimate for hedging (eg egress between zones). Added suggestion to limit hedging to high-priority API keys.
Maya L. Chen (2026-02-24): Honor per-tenant hedging opt-in via tenant config; docs updated.
Evan Zhou (2026-02-25): perf bench looks good. One question: fallback rollout uses the same rollout controller - ensure it doesn't trigger canary alerts. Added approval pending small test addition.
Maya L. Chen (2026-02-26): Added test to ensure fallback rollouts are labeled emergency and do not count towards normal canary metrics. Ready for merge.
release_notes: Adds SLO-driven phased node eviction and cross-zone hedging to reduce p99 latency during node-level GPU degradations. Includes KV-cache rebind fix and operator playbook. Rollout gated behind feature flags.
notes: Canary run in internal staging for 72h. Monitor slo_drain_phase transitions and error budget burn closely during next scheduled maintenance window.
